subject: Key-control playbook & BYOK logistics — follow-up from demo
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@fintrust.com>, security-eng@fintrust.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Key-control playbook & BYOK logistics — follow-up from demo

Hi Liam / FinTrust security team,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the thoughtful questions from your crypto team. This thread is a concise recap plus a few clarifying questions so we can scope the workshop + SOW accurately. Attaching a short template to capture your requirements (encryption-requirements-template.xlsx) and an overview of our BYOK options.

Quick recap (what we covered):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced, option for mTLS for service-to-service calls.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM server-side encryption; optional customer-managed keys (BYOK).
- Key custody: support for cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK / Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed customer-managed keys (CloudHSM or HSM in Private deployment).
- Logging & audit: audit trails for key ops, request-level telemetry; can forward logs to customer SIEM.
- Data residency: model serving region controls and isolated Private deployment for on-prem/VPC.

Clarifying questions (so we scope correctly):
1) Do you require HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 / FIPS 140-3) for workload encryption, or will KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys suffice?
2) If HSM is required, does FinTrust require the HSM cluster to be in your VPC (Private deployment) or is a dedicated CloudHSM cluster in our account acceptable?
3) Desired key rotation cadence (we heard ~12 months on the call — confirm).
4) Audit log retention requirement (you mentioned long-term retention — please confirm years and whether logs must be exportable to Splunk/S3/GCS).
5) Access model: do you need split custody / dual-control for key deletion or purely role-based access?

Next steps we propose:
- Share the filled encryption template (attached) with answers to the Qs above.
- Schedule a 60-minute crypto ops workshop (we'll bring our security engineering lead) to walk through the architecture options.
- We’ll produce a short SOW stub outlining the Private vs BYOK implementation paths and a high-level timeline and indicative pricing.

Attachments: encryption-requirements-template.xlsx, redwood-byok-overview.pdf

Thanks — I’ll ping calendar options once we get your preferred times.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

---
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@fintrust.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security-eng@fintrust.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:06:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Key-control playbook & BYOK logistics — follow-up from demo

Soojin — thanks for the recap and the template. A few answers from our side to help you prepare the workshop and SOW: 

- HSM requirement: We require HSM-backed key material for all customer-managed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or equivalent). CloudHSM is acceptable only if the HSMs are dedicated and can be audited by our team.
- Deployment: Prefer HSM within our VPC (Private deploy) for production; for PoC we can consider a dedicated CloudHSM cluster.
- Rotation: 12 months is our baseline; can be shorter for higher-sensitivity keys.
- Audit & retention: We need key operation logs and request-level telemetry forwarded to our Splunk instance with 7-year retention. Logs should be exportable as JSON and include request ID, calling principal, and timestamp.
- Access controls: Dual-approval for key deletion and high-privilege ops; RBAC for daily ops.

Additionally we need:
- A sample runbook that shows key creation, rotation, compromise procedures, and cross-region key replication behavior.
- SOC 2 Type II evidence related to key handling and logging (we will accept redacted artifacts).
- A proposed SOW and an initial estimate for the Private deployment + HSM option, and incremental pricing if we opt for a hosted BYOK path.

Can Marissa / Karthik include rough lead times for Private deployment + HSM provisioning? We need that to align procurement.

Cheers,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Security Engineering | FinTrust
liam@fintrust.com

Copying myself in on the thread. Action items I captured: 
- Karthik: draft options matrix (CloudHSM dedicated vs Private HSM-in-VPC) with provisioning lead times and price deltas.
- Karthik & SE infra: confirm whether dual-approval workflows for key deletion are supported out-of-the-box or require a small engineering task.
- Soojin: schedule workshop with Liam / crypto ops (send calendar options and attach SOW stub).
- Marketing / Legal: prepare redacted SOC2 artifact and a short statement about our key auditability.

Karthik — can you estimate lead times by EOD tomorrow? I’ll get the SOW stub edited and share.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@fintrust.com>, security-eng@fintrust.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Key-control playbook & BYOK logistics — follow-up from demo

Liam — thanks for the quick answers, appreciate the clarity. Short responses inline and next steps below.

- HSM requirement: Confirmed — we support HSM-backed key material. Production-grade option is Redwood Private with customer HSM in your VPC; for PoC we can provision a dedicated CloudHSM cluster (audit access can be arranged).
- Deployment: Private deployment (HSM inside customer VPC) is our recommended path for your requirement set.
- Rotation: 12 months supported; we can parameterize to shorter windows and automate rotation workflows.
- Audit & retention: We can stream key-op and request logs to your Splunk instance via a secure forwarder; logs can be exported as JSON. We’ll include a retention/export play in the SOW (default: 7 years per your note).
- Access controls: Dual-approval (two-person) gating for destructive ops is supported via an integration with our identity provider and a small policy config — engineering effort estimated ~1-2 SUs.

Attachments included: redwood-byok-overview.pdf, redwood-sow-stub.docx (SOW contains two tracks: Hosted BYOK and Private+HSM with indicative lead times).

Proposed near-term plan:
1) Please complete the encryption-requirements-template.xlsx with any additional constraints, then upload to the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/FT-202704/encryption-requirements
2) Workshop: proposed slots — Tue Apr 20 10:00-11:00 ET or Wed Apr 21 14:00-15:00 ET. Calendar link: https://calendly.com/soojin-lee/redwood-crypto-workshop-60m
3) Karthik / Marissa will follow with a brief options matrix and estimated provisioning lead time (Private HSM lead time typically 4–6 weeks depending on procurement).
4) We’ll produce a draft SOW and pricing matrix within 48 business hours after we get your filled template.

If that plan works, I’ll lock the workshop and start the SOW edits.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-byok-overview.pdf (15 KB), redwood-sow-stub.docx (42 KB)
